subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency/throughput decision follow-up
messages:

Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — follow-up & next steps

Hi Priya — great to meet today, and thanks for walking through FinPay's payment routing use case. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can recommend the right deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity vs Private VPC).

Recap:
- Primary workload: real-time payment routing and fraud scoring for web + mobile.
- Expected steady-state: ~30 requests/sec across peak regions.
- Latency target: p95 <= 250ms for synchronous user-facing calls.
- Spike profile: batch settlement jobs + marketing spikes can cause short bursts up to ~500 req/s for 5–15 minutes.
- Data sensitivity: PCI-adjacent, currently okay with redacted PII, but evaluating stricter isolation later.

Clarifying questions:
1) Are the 30 req/s numbers per region or global? If regional, which regions are critical? 
2) For the burst cases (500 r/s), are those user-facing synchronous requests or async batch jobs we can queue?
3) Any hard SLOs for tail latency during bursts, or is graceful degradation acceptable (e.g., fallback to async)?

Next steps I suggest:
- If steady-state latency + predictable throughput are primary, Dedicated is typically the right fit.
- For fast time-to-value and smaller initial spend, Hosted can work with burst protections (rate limits, fallback) while we size Dedicated.
- We'll run a short benchmark/POC to show p95 latency and cost per 1M tokens on Dedicated vs Hosted for your exact payloads.

I'll wait for the three clarifications above; I can pull together an initial bench matrix and a mutual action plan (MAP) once we confirm. Attaching a short template MAP to this thread.

Thanks,
Dylan

Thanks, Dylan — this is helpful. Quick answers below.

1) The 30 req/s is global steady-state; regional peaks are primarily US-east and EU-west (US-east ~60% of traffic).
2) The 500 req/s spikes are a mix — roughly 70% are user-facing (promo windows) and 30% are async batch jobs. Spikes last ~10 minutes.
3) Hard SLOs: user-facing p95 should stay under 350ms where possible. For promo spikes, we can accept short degradation to ~500ms if it buys stability.

Important: predictability of throughput and cost is a driver for the execs — they prefer reserved predictable pricing if latency is guaranteed. Security is important but not yet demanding a VPC/on-prem setup.

Can you confirm whether Dedicated provides automatic burst capacity or if we need a hybrid approach (Dedicated + Hosted overflow)? Also, does Redwood provide a recommended configuration (GPU type, concurrency) for 30 req/s steady-state with those burst shapes?

Appreciate the help — Priya

Priya Raj

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated — follow-up & next steps

Thanks for the details — very helpful.

Recommendation (short): Dedicated reserved capacity + Hosted overflow for short marketing spikes.

Why:
- Dedicated gives predictable throughput and consistent p95 latency under steady load (30 req/s) and is cost-efficient for long-running workloads.
- For short promo spikes (~10 minutes) you can configure automatic burst policies (burst buckets + short-term autoscale) on Dedicated, but very large instantaneous spikes are often best handled with a configured overflow to Hosted to avoid scaling cold-starts.

Sizing guidance (initial):
- GPU profile: 1x A10/NVIDIA L4-class instance pool for the model family you're evaluating (we'll confirm exact model and quantization). That profile handles ~40–60 concurrency with p95 around 120–220ms depending on sequence length.
- Dedicated capacity: reserve enough to cover steady-state concurrency for 30 req/s (approx 2–4 GPU units depending on batching and sequence length). We'll validate with your payloads.
- Burst strategy: configure short-term autoscale to add capacity over ~3–5 minutes + a Hosted overflow token bucket for short spikes. This keeps latency predictable without large reserved overhead.

Benchmarks: I attached an initial benchmark csv using a synthetic payload similar to what we discussed. It includes p50/p95 for Hosted vs Dedicated and estimated cost/month for steady-state. See benchmark_results.csv.

Next steps:
1) We'll schedule a 2-hour POC run where we replay representative traffic (steady + spike) against dedicated sizing options.
2) Marissa will follow up on commercials and a draft MAP. 

Looping Marissa to start pricing and POA.

-Dylan

Commercial ranges (ballpark for budgeting):
- Hosted API (pay-as-you-go): good for initial tests; estimated steady-state cost ~ $1.8k–$2.5k/month for your 30 req/s profile (depends on model and tokens).
- Dedicated (reserved monthly): estimated commit $6k–$9k/month depending on GPU type and reservation term — provides ~3x better predictability and lower unit cost at scale.

Proposed MAP (high level):
1) POC (2 weeks): replay traffic + 1-week observation (Dylan + Engs). Deliverable: latency/throughput report + config recommendation.
2) Pilot (1 month): deploy Dedicated with autoscale + Hosted overflow, monitor for promo spikes.
